name: Warwickshire
description: Warwickshire is a historic county in the West Midlands famous for its connections to William Shakespeare and the town of Stratford-upon-Avon. It combines fertile countryside with historic towns such as Warwick and industrial centres such as Nuneaton and Rugby.

places.name: North Warwickshire
places.description: A rural district in Warwickshire mixing former coalfield villages with open countryside, sitting close to the historic town of Atherstone.

places.name: Nuneaton and Bedworth
places.description: A former mining and textile district in Warwickshire, birthplace of novelist George Eliot, who drew heavily on the local landscape in her writing.

places.name: Rugby
places.description: A market town in Warwickshire that gave its name to rugby football, said to have been invented at Rugby School in 1823 when a pupil picked up the ball and ran with it.

places.name: Stratford-on-Avon
places.description: A district in Warwickshire built around the market town of Stratford-upon-Avon, birthplace of William Shakespeare and home to the Royal Shakespeare Company.

places.name: Warwick
places.description: The county town of Warwickshire, dominated by Warwick Castle, one of England's best-preserved medieval fortresses, now a major visitor attraction.
